1.2mm Microfiber PU Leather for Bags (Wholesale)

Our 1.2mm microfiber PU leather is engineered for handbag, backpack, and small leather goods producers who need a tear-resistant skin that still skives, folds, and edges like a premium hide. As a factory supplying microfiber PU leather wholesale to bag makers across Europe, North America, and Southeast Asia, we run this base cloth at 54-58" (137-147 cm) width on continuous rolls so your cutting tables waste less between nests. This page lays out the exact specs, certifications, and ordering terms our bag clients ask for before they place a sampling order.

Microfiber synthetic leather differs from ordinary PU on a knit or woven backing: the base is a needle-punched non-woven of ultra-fine polyamide filaments impregnated with polyurethane, which is why it carries a leather-like grain, holds stitch tension, and resists delamination far better than coated fabric. For bags that get yanked, stuffed, and dropped, that structural difference is the whole point.

Because the polyamide microfiber bundles are distributed evenly through the full cross-section, the cut edge looks dense rather than foamy, and edge paint adheres without a separate sealing primer on most colors. That saves a step on the bench and reduces edge cracking after the bag is in use.

Why Choose Microfiber Over Standard PU for Bags?

Bag makers come to microfiber PU leather wholesale supply when ordinary coated PU starts failing in the field, usually at corners, handle roots, and zipper tape. Here is how the two compare on the points that drive returns:

  • Stitch tear-out: the non-woven base anchors thread far better than a 2-3 ply knit backing, so handle attachments and gusset seams hold under load instead of zippering open.
  • Delamination: microfiber is impregnated, not laminated, so there is no skin-to-fabric glue line to peel; this is why peel values sit at 28-40 N/25mm rather than the 10-18 N/25mm typical of cheap coated PU.
  • Grain memory: embossed grains stay crisp after folding and creasing, which matters for structured totes and flap bags.
  • Hand and weight: at 620-740 g/m² it feels substantial without the rubbery stiffness of PVC, and it skives cleanly for turned edges.
  • Abrasion: 40,000-100,000 Martindale cycles keeps the grain intact through years of daily carry, versus the visible scuffing standard PU shows by 15,000-20,000.

If you are still mapping the full material landscape before you commit, our guide to types of synthetic leather and how to choose walks through where microfiber, regular PU, and PVC each make sense by application and budget.

Certifications and Compliance

Bags sold into the EU, US, and California retail channels need a defensible compliance file. Our 1.2mm bag-grade microfiber ships with documentation covering the regimes below; we issue lot-specific test reports on request so your import paperwork matches the goods on the water.

  • REACH (EC 1907/2006) SVHC screening on the candidate list in force at production date.
  • RoHS restricted-substance limits for heavy metals and phthalates.
  • OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Class II articles, suitable for items in direct skin contact such as handle wraps and strap pads.
  • California Proposition 65 screening for listed substances relevant to consumer leather goods.

We do not claim certifications we cannot evidence. Each test report names the accredited lab, the method, and the sampled lot, so your QC and customs brokers can verify rather than take our word for it. For the regulatory and durability fundamentals behind these claims, see our deeper reference on whether PU leather is durable and waterproof.

Color, Grain, and Finishing Options

Bag programs live and die on color matching and grain consistency, so this is where most of our pre-production work goes. Standard offerings:

  • Grains: fine pebble, litchi, saffiano cross-hatch, smooth nappa, and full-grain calf emboss.
  • Finishes: matte, semi-matte, and pearlized top-coats; soft-touch and anti-scratch top-coats for premium lines.
  • Color: match to Pantone TCX or a physical swatch; we hold lot-to-lot color difference within ΔE ≤ 1.0 under D65.
  • Backing: raw microfiber back, or a brushed/suede back for clients who want a finished interior without lining.

Lab dips and embossed strike-offs take 7-10 days. We keep approved master swatches sealed and bar-coded so a re-order eighteen months later still matches the original handbag run.

Frequently Asked Sourcing Questions

Can I order below the 300 m MOQ for a capsule collection? We can sometimes release a 100-150 m short run from an in-stock color at a unit surcharge; new custom colors hold the 300 m floor because of dye-batch economics.

Does microfiber pass the bag-industry crock and flex tests? Yes. Standard lots return Grade 4-5 dry crocking and survive 50,000+ flex cycles at room temperature without grain cracking; we will run a specific flex-fold protocol if your retailer mandates one.

How does this compare to genuine leather for a mid-tier bag? Microfiber gives consistent thickness across the whole roll, no flaws or bug-bite scars to cut around, and a stable cost, while genuine hide brings patina and brand story. Our breakdown of PU leather versus genuine leather sourcing covers the trade-offs lot by lot.

Send us your grain, color reference, and target unit cost, and we will return a spec sheet, a current test report, and a sampling timeline within two business days.
